Price is assumed flat so the comparison isolates the pure dividend-compounding effect; taxes and fees are not modeled.

Educational estimates only — not financial advice.

📖 How to use

  1. Enter the initial investment, dividend yield and dividend growth rate.
  2. Set the time horizon and toggle DRIP on or off.
  3. Compare ending values side by side.

❓ Frequently asked questions

How does DRIP compounding work?

With DRIP, each dividend buys more shares, so the next dividend is larger — compounding on compounding. Cash payouts keep the share count fixed.

What is dividend growth in this model?

Each year the dividend yield applies to the current value, and the yield itself grows by the dividend-growth rate you enter.

When does DRIP make the biggest difference?

Higher yield with high growth and long horizons favors DRIP most; over decades the gap can be several multiples.
